If a gate agent tries to hand you a voucher, do not touch their screen. Say this instead:

"I am not giving up my seat voluntarily. Under DOT regulation 14 CFR 250.5, involuntary denied boarding requires a 400% payout of my one-way fare, up to $1,550 by check or instant transfer today. I decline the credit. Please hand me the written statement of my DOT rights and process the payout."

Gate agents are trained to get your signature fast because once you accept a voucher, the airline legally erases their $1,550 penalty.

If an airline sells your seat twice to make extra profit, it is completely legal. If you skip the last leg of a connecting flight to save $100, they cancel your ticket and ban you.

Have you ever been tricked into taking a voucher instead of a payout?

note_tweet.text:
OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet on Nov. 13, 2026, allowing ChatGPT “dots” agents to complete merchant checkouts after user approval. It is initially rolling out to US ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18 and older with eligible US-issued credit cards.

Users approve every purchase with Face ID, Touch ID or similar biometrics. Card networks then issue a payment token with separate card details; OpenAI says it receives only limited information, such as the last four digits, not the full card number or security code.

Merchants do not need a Wallet-specific integration, but OpenAI asks them to allow its signed cloud browser through firewalls and adjust fraud systems to avoid declining agent purchases. The merchant remains the seller of record, while the card issuer handles charges and disputes.

The launch uses existing card rails. OpenAI’s launch materials do not mention stablecoins or crypto.
